clue.text: Early visitor yesterday for tots — fire blazing?

indicators.note: something blazing is in wild, flaring disorder, so the words before it are thrown into a new order

blocks.note: three words taken as written as the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A New Year guest bringing drinks for the little ones while the fire roars.
explanation.walkthrough: The puzzle appeared just after New Year's Day, hence 'yesterday'. 'Tots' suggests drams of whisky, fitting the Hogmanay scene.
explanation.definitionFit: In Scottish custom the first-footer is the first person to cross the threshold after midnight on New Year's Eve, an early-morning visitor on 1 January.

clue.text: As if Mrs Thatcher could be Santa!

indicators.note: could be says these letters may turn into something else once rearranged

blocks.note: the opening words taken as written, all fifteen letters

explanation.surface: A joke at the idea of the Iron Lady playing the jolly gift-giver.
explanation.walkthrough: Margaret Thatcher was the British Prime Minister of the 1980s; the absurdity of her as Santa hides the fact that her name holds every letter needed.
explanation.definitionFit: Father Christmas is the traditional British name for Santa Claus, the bearded bringer of presents.

clue.text: Play associated with one girl in a world of romance?

blocks.note: R.U.R. is Karel Capek's 1920 play about robots
the Roman numeral for one
a girl's name

explanation.surface: A drama linked to a young woman in some imagined realm of love stories.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Play' looks like a verb or a general word for drama; it is one particular play, R.U.R., which gave the world the word robot.
explanation.definitionFit: Ruritania is the fictional central European kingdom of Anthony Hope's The Prisoner of Zenda, a byword for swashbuckling romantic adventure.

clue.text: Style of architecture identified by duke in the course of organised tour

indicators.note: something organised has been put into a fresh arrangement, so the letters of the last word are reordered
in the course of puts one thing partway through another, so it sits inside

blocks.note: taken as written, then rearranged
D is the standard abbreviation for duke

explanation.surface: A guide on a coach trip points out a building style, with a nobleman along for the ride.
explanation.definitionFit: Tudor architecture is the half-timbered English building style of the period 1485 to 1603.

clue.text: In seventh heaven, as Hillary once was?

blocks.note: first meaning: blissfully happy, elated
second meaning, literal: standing on the summit of Everest, as Edmund Hillary did in 1953

explanation.walkthrough: Sir Edmund Hillary and Tenzing Norgay were the first to reach the summit of Everest, the world's highest point.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom for elation also literally describes someone standing on the highest peak on Earth.

clue.text: One who has dealings with a US lorry driver?

blocks.note: first meaning: someone who barters or trades, from the old verb truck, to exchange goods
second meaning: an American driver of heavy goods vehicles

explanation.surface: Someone doing business with an American haulier.
explanation.definitionFit: To truck is an old verb for trading or bartering, and in America a truck is a lorry, so its driver bears the same name.

clue.text: Witty retort about accepting one appointment

indicators.note: accepting means taking something in, so one part holds the others within it

blocks.note: re means about or concerning
the Roman numeral for one
a post is a job or appointment

explanation.surface: A clever comeback on the subject of taking up a job.
explanation.definitionFit: A riposte is a quick, sharp reply, originally a fencer's counter-thrust.

clue.text: Yell in brief violent storm

blocks.note: first meaning: to cry out loudly, as a baby does
second meaning: a sudden fierce gust of wind with rain

explanation.surface: Shouting during a short, fierce downpour.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a verb for crying out harshly and a noun for a sudden gusty storm at sea.

clue.text: Graduate reportedly takes in a network of circuit elements

indicators.note: reportedly means as heard said, so the spelling follows a sound

blocks.note: a Master of Arts
to take in is to fool or deceive

explanation.surface: A university graduate is said to absorb a whole grid of electronic components.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Takes in' looks like a container signal; here it means deceives.
explanation.definitionFit: In electronics a matrix is a grid-like array of interconnected circuit elements.

clue.text: Billeted in lodgings in district, extremely exposed

indicators.note: extremely points to the extremes of the word, its first and last letters

blocks.note: a quarter is a district of a city
just the two end letters of this word

explanation.surface: Soldiers put up in rooms in a part of town where they are left very vulnerable.
explanation.definitionFit: To quarter troops is to house them, so soldiers quartered are lodged, as when billeted.

clue.text: Whack team's leader on shoulder

indicators.note: a leader comes at the front, so only the opening letter is wanted

blocks.note: the first letter of team
a hump is a rounded bulge, like a hunched shoulder or the shoulder of a hill

explanation.surface: Slapping the captain on the shoulder.
explanation.definitionFit: A thump is a heavy blow, the same as a whack.

clue.text: Go along with a European, for the most part

indicators.note: for the most part means not all of it, so the word loses its final letter

blocks.note: taken as written
a Greek is a European

explanation.surface: Mostly accompanying someone from Europe.
explanation.definitionFit: To go along with an idea is to consent to it, which is to agree.

clue.text: UK rep isn't prepared for these US motorways

indicators.note: something prepared has been worked up into a new form, so the letters before it are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written, apostrophe dropped

explanation.surface: A British sales rep is not ready for American highways.
explanation.definitionFit: In the United States a turnpike is a toll expressway, the equivalent of a major motorway.

clue.text: One prisoner is after law dictionary

indicators.note: is after says these pieces follow the law piece in the word, not precede it

blocks.note: lex is Latin for law
the Roman numeral for one
a con is a convict

explanation.surface: An inmate is chasing up a legal reference book.
explanation.definitionFit: A lexicon is a dictionary, especially of an ancient language, or the vocabulary of a subject.

clue.text: Valid gen given by sappers round about

indicators.note: round means encircling, so one piece goes around the other

blocks.note: gen is British slang for information
the Royal Engineers, whose soldiers are called sappers
c is short for circa, about

explanation.surface: Army engineers pass around the information that is currently correct.
explanation.definitionFit: A rule in force is in effect and binding, so it is valid.

clue.text: Ones entering one Asian republic from another

indicators.note: entering means going inside, so the first word sits within the other

blocks.note: a different Asian republic from the one defined
taken as written

explanation.surface: People crossing into one Asian country from a neighbouring one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Another' stands for a second Asian republic, which the solver must pick.
explanation.definitionFit: Indonesia is a republic of islands in south-east Asia.

clue.text: Army officer caught out on a Mediterranean island

blocks.note: a major is an army rank
c is the scorecard mark for a cricket dismissal by catching
taken as written

explanation.surface: A military man is dismissed while on holiday on a Spanish island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Out' looks like an anagram signal; 'caught out' is the cricket dismissal, written c on a scorecard.
explanation.definitionFit: Majorca, or Mallorca, is the largest of Spain's Balearic Islands in the Mediterranean.

clue.text: Benefit from travel allowance

blocks.note: first meaning: advantage or use, as in getting good value out of something
second meaning: money paid per mile driven on business

explanation.surface: Profiting from the expenses paid for journeys.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both the advantage drawn from something and an allowance paid for each mile travelled.

clue.text: Painted woman, Biblical character

blocks.note: first meaning: a shameless, heavily made-up woman
second meaning: the wicked queen of Ahab in the Book of Kings

explanation.surface: A heavily made-up figure from scripture.
explanation.definitionFit: Queen Jezebel painted her face before her death, so her name became a byword for a brazen woman.

clue.text: Period of time touring in the old country?

indicators.note: touring means going all around, so the period wraps about the other piece

blocks.note: a day is a period of time
to be in is to be at home

explanation.surface: A spell spent travelling around the land of one's birth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The old country' suggests one's homeland; the question mark flags a country with an old name.
explanation.definitionFit: Dahomey was the former name of the West African state now called Benin, a country under an obsolete title.

clue.text: Very angry over international being reckless

indicators.note: in a down entry over means placed above, so the first piece comes on top

blocks.note: mad means furious
a cap is a player chosen for their national team

explanation.surface: A national team player is furious about his own rashness.
explanation.definitionFit: Madcap describes wild, impulsive behaviour, so it is a synonym of reckless.

clue.text: French girl almost checked out after end of party

indicators.note: end of picks out the final letter of the word that follows
almost means not quite all, so the last letter is dropped

blocks.note: the final letter of party
to vet is to check someone out

explanation.surface: A young woman from France has nearly finished inspecting things once the party is over.
explanation.definitionFit: Yvette is a French female first name.

clue.text: Slow-moving girl bringing tray

blocks.note: lazy means sluggish
a girl's name

explanation.surface: A sluggish young woman carrying in a serving tray.
explanation.definitionFit: A lazy Susan is a revolving tray placed in the centre of a table for serving food.

clue.text: Small book drawing attention to Aegean island

blocks.note: S is the clothing-size abbreviation for small
Amos is a book of the Old Testament

explanation.surface: A little guidebook promoting a Greek holiday island.
explanation.definitionFit: Samos is a Greek island in the eastern Aegean, birthplace of Pythagoras.

clue.text: Lofted club might get Woosnam's first on fringe

indicators.note: first says only the opening letter of the name is used
on here means placed against, so one piece is set directly before the other

blocks.note: the initial of Ian Woosnam, the Welsh golfer
an edge is a fringe or border

explanation.surface: A golfer playing from the edge of the green reaches for a high-lofted iron.
explanation.walkthrough: Ian Woosnam won the 1991 US Masters; 'fringe' is also golf's word for the collar of grass around the green, adding to the scene.
explanation.definitionFit: A wedge is a golf iron with a steeply angled face for lofting the ball high.

clue.text: Record shown in book

blocks.note: first meaning: an LP or collection of recorded tracks
second meaning: a blank book for photos, stamps or autographs

explanation.surface: A record set down in a written volume.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a set of tracks released together and a book for keeping photographs or stamps.

clue.text: Terrible crimes — social worker exposes wrongdoer

indicators.note: terrible suggests something mangled and awful, so the next word's letters are jumbled

blocks.note: taken as written, then rearranged
an ant is a worker in a social insect colony

explanation.surface: A welfare officer unmasks a villain behind dreadful offences.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Social worker' reads as a welfare officer; it is an insect from a social colony.
explanation.definitionFit: A miscreant is someone who behaves badly or breaks the law, a villain.

clue.text: British essayist, one's to come to shore after leaving US entry station

blocks.note: Havelock Ellis, the British essayist and writer on sexuality
one is I, so one's (one is) gives I plus S
to land is to come ashore

explanation.surface: A writer is due to step ashore after a voyage, arriving in America.
explanation.definitionFit: Ellis Island in New York harbour was the main immigration station through which arrivals entered the United States.
